about.title: About Orbisol
about.what: Orbisol helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies using NASA Earth observations, local soil information, crop characteristics and their own priorities.
about.ai: Built with AI assistance (Claude by Anthropic) for code and documentation drafts. The idea and decisions are the author's.
about.event: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data
about.osm: Coastline overlay: NASA GIBS reference layer, © OpenStreetMap contributors.

season.window: {{from}} to {{to}} ({{days}} days), compared with the same days in {{bFrom}}–{{bTo}} ({{n}} years).
season.loading: Getting NASA data for your field… (first time about 1 MB, then saved on this phone)
season.error: Could not get NASA data for this field right now. Check your internet and try again.

origin.static: Built-in data for the demo region

season.hotThreshold: Hot day here means above {{t}} °C: the hottest 10% of these days in {{bFrom}}–{{bTo}}.

hotDays.name: Hot days
hotDays.what: Days hotter than usual for this time of year. Many hot days can stress crops and raise water use.

rainTotal.name: Rain
rainTotal.what: Total rain that fell in this window.

heavyRainDays.name: Extreme rain days
heavyRainDays.what: Days with 20 mm of rain or more. These can flood fields, wash away soil and damage crops.

frostDays.name: Frost days
frostDays.what: Nights when the air 2 m above ground fell below 0 °C.

soilWetness.name: Soil moisture (top layer)
soilWetness.what: How much of the space in the top few centimetres of soil holds water: 0% is bone dry, 100% is soaked. From a NASA model that does not include canal irrigation, so irrigated fields are wetter than shown.

waterBalance.name: Water balance
waterBalance.what: Rain minus evaporation demand. Below zero means the air took more water than rain gave; canal water or stored soil water had to fill the gap.

greenness.name: Greenness (NDVI)
greenness.what: How green and leafy plants look from space. Low greenness can mean stress, bare soil or harvest.

et0Total.name: Evaporation demand (ET0)
et0Total.what: How much water a healthy, well-watered grass field would lose to the air (reference evapotranspiration, FAO-56). Hot, dry, windy, sunny days raise it. Most crops need about this much water or more.

season.gap: Data gap: satellite greenness is not loaded yet for this field.
season.frostFlag: ground frost can happen even when the air stays just above 0 °C
season.rainFlag: canal water is not in these numbers; your canal turn matters more than rain here
season.sure1: Weather numbers come from NASA POWER, a model on a grid of about 50 km. They describe your area, not your exact field, and they do not include canal irrigation.
season.sure2: Normal is the middle value (median) of the same days in {{n}} past years. The usual range covers the middle 80% of those years.
season.sure3: Above or below normal means this window was in the top or bottom third of those years.
season.coverage: Days with data in this window: {{pct}}%.
season.sure4: Evaporation demand from this model grid may read higher than at a local weather station in canal-irrigated areas, because the model does not see the cooler, more humid air over irrigated fields. Compare it with normal rather than reading it as an exact amount.

why.existing: This is your current rotation: the baseline the others are compared with.
why.betterFor: Scores better than your current rotation on "{{priority}}", one of your priorities.
why.balanced: A balanced option for your priorities; it does not beat your current rotation on any single one.

evidence.waterNeed: {{crop}} needs about {{mm}} mm of water over its season (range {{low}}–{{high}} mm): FAO-56 crop coefficient × evaporation demand at your field.
evidence.et0Source: Evaporation demand (ET0) is the 1991–2020 daily average from NASA POWER weather data at your field.
evidence.bareDays: Field bare about {{days}} days a year, {{hot}} of them in the hottest months.

benefit.lessWater: About {{pct}}% less crop water need than your current rotation.
benefit.moreCover: Field covered about {{days}} more days a year: less bare soil for wind and water to erode.
benefit.lessBareInHeat: {{days}} fewer bare days in the hottest months.
benefit.nitrogen: {{crop}} adds nitrogen to the soil (legume), which can help the next crop.
benefit.pestBreak: Brings in a new plant family ({{families}}). A different host can interrupt pests and diseases that live on one family.

gap.market: Market prices and demand are not in Orbisol. Check local buyers before switching.
gap.varieties: Variety choice and seed availability are not modelled.
gap.proxyStages: {{crop}} growth stages borrow a similar crop's FAO-56 values.
gap.forage: Fodder value of {{crop}} residues is not counted (no source found).
gap.sowingSource: {{crop}} sowing dates come from a general source; check with your local agriculture office.
gap.irrigationModel: Weather data comes from a NASA model that does not see canal irrigation.

risk.saltSensitive: {{crop}} is salt-sensitive ({{rating}}; yield starts to fall above ECe {{ece}} dS/m). You said your soil is salty.

vulnerable.hot: {{crop}} is in a sensitive stage during the hottest months ({{months}}).
vulnerable.frost: {{crop}} is in a sensitive stage in frost-prone months ({{months}}).
vulnerable.heavyRain: {{crop}} is in a sensitive stage when heavy rain is most frequent ({{months}}).

risk.overlap: Crops overlap by {{days}} days: the next crop must be sown into the last one (relay sowing) or later than shown.
risk.moreWater: Needs about {{pct}}% more water than your current rotation.
risk.moreBare: Field is bare {{days}} more days a year ({{hot}} bare days in the hottest months): more erosion and weeds.
risk.newCrop: {{crop}} is new to this rotation: seed, skills, machinery and buyers need checking.
risk.tightTurnaround: Less than a week between the previous harvest and sowing {{crop}}.

farm.title: My farm
farm.intro: Tell Orbisol how you farm now. Everything is saved on this phone.
farm.rotationHint: Crops in the order you grow them in one year.
farm.prioritiesHint: Tap up to 3, most important first.
farm.judgment: you know your field's history, pests and buyers better than any satellite

rotations.title: Compare rotations
rotations.intro: Your current rotation and the two options that fit your priorities best.
rotations.weightsHint: 1st counts 3×, 2nd 2×, 3rd 1×. Tap to change; the ranking updates at once.
rotations.marketNote: Market suitability is never scored (no price data). It always needs local review.
rotations.noPriorities: No priorities chosen: all scored priorities count equally.
rotations.mmEstimate: Crop water need ≈ {{mm}} mm a year (range {{low}}–{{high}}): estimate, likely high (see limitations).
rotations.tradeoffNone: No trade-off found on these measures.
rotations.scoresTitle: How it scores on your priorities
rotations.scoresHint: 100% = the best of all rotations Orbisol checked for this field.

calendar.title: Seasonal calendar
calendar.intro: Your current rotation month by month: when the field is bare and when crops look vulnerable.
calendar.bareHot: {{days}} of the bare days fall in the hottest months.
calendar.climateSource: Hottest months, heavy rain and frost: NASA POWER, 1991–2020 normals at your field.
calendar.noHazards: No frost or frequent heavy-rain months here.
calendar.judgment: actual sowing and harvest dates vary year to year

outlook.title: Season Twins
outlook.intro: Past years whose same days looked most like this season, and what happened in the {{days}} days after.
outlook.notInformative: Not informative here: this outcome hardly changes from year to year.
outlook.track: Track record: tested on {{n}} past years using only earlier years, right {{hits}} times ({{rate}}%). Always guessing the usual answer: {{base}}%.
outlook.greenNote: Greenness in twin years arrives with the satellite (MODIS / VIIRS) data.

confidence.noTwins: No similar past years were found.
confidence.twinsClose: Twin years are very similar to this season (difference {{d}}).
confidence.twinsFar: Twin years are not very similar (difference {{d}}).
confidence.trackSmallSkill: Past tests only slightly beat guessing ({{hit}}% vs {{base}}%).
confidence.trackNoSkill: Past tests did no better than guessing ({{hit}}% vs {{base}}%).
